pattern: improper delimiter validation
fix: Updated parse_header, get_header_lines, and ChunkedReceiver.received to use CRLF as the delimiter and added checks for bare CR or LF in header lines.
guard: The check for b"\r" in first_line or b"\n" in first_line in parse_header.
lesson: Always use the standard CRLF delimiter for HTTP protocol parsing and validate against illegal bare line breaks.

regression.given: A request with a header line containing a bare LF or CR
regression.then: A ParsingError is raised

symptom.text: The parser would silently ignore invalid or multiple Content-Length headers by defaulting the value to zero.

root_cause.text: A ValueError during integer conversion of the Content-Length header was caught and suppressed by setting the length to zero.

pattern: suppressing errors during type conversion
fix: The function parse_header was modified to raise a ParsingError instead of defaulting to zero when a ValueError occurs.
guard: the ParsingError raise in parse_header
lesson: Do not swallow conversion errors that indicate malformed protocol headers.

regression.given: a request with a non-integer content-length or multiple content-length headers
regression.then: a ParsingError with the message 'Content-Length is invalid' is raised

symptom.text: The server might not correctly signal that a requested transfer encoding is unsupported, or might fail to handle multiple transfer-encoding values correctly.

root_cause.text: The parser only checked if the transfer-encoding string was exactly 'chunked', failing to properly validate lists of encodings or unsupported types.

pattern: improper validation of delimited list values
fix: In parse_header, the code now splits the TRANSFER_ENCODING header by commas, iterates through all encodings to ensure only 'chunked' is used, and raises TransferEncodingNotImplemented if any other encoding is present. In received, TransferEncodingNotImplemented is caught to set the error to ServerNotImplemented.
guard: The loop in parse_header checking if encoding not in {'chunked'}
lesson: When parsing comma-separated header values, validate every element in the list against a whitelist.

regression.given: A request with an unsupported transfer-encoding like 'gzip' or multiple encodings including an unsupported one
regression.then: A TransferEncodingNotImplemented exception is raised and the server returns a 501 ServerNotImplemented error

symptom.text: The parser might strip non-printable or invalid whitespace characters from header values, potentially allowing request smuggling.

root_cause.text: Using the default strip() method removes all whitespace characters, including non-printable characters like \x85, which are not valid whitespace according to RFC7230.

pattern: overly aggressive whitespace stripping
fix: The strip() method was replaced with strip(b" \t") in parse_header and strip(" \t") in the transfer-encoding encoding loop.
guard: The strip function in parse_header and the encoding loop now only target space and tab characters.
lesson: Only strip characters explicitly defined as whitespace by the relevant protocol specification.

regression.given: A request with Transfer-Encoding containing invalid whitespace like \x85 or unicode characters like \xe2\x84\xaa
regression.then: A TransferEncodingNotImplemented error is raised

symptom.text: An object could be created with a modified prototype via the __proto__ key.

root_cause.text: The clone function iterated over keys including __proto__ without filtering them.

pattern: prototype pollution via property injection
fix: The internals.clone function was updated to skip the __proto__ key during iteration.
guard: The check 'if (key === '__proto__') { continue; }' in internals.clone.
lesson: Always sanitize or skip sensitive keys like __proto__ when cloning objects.

regression.given: an object parsed from JSON containing a __proto__ property
regression.then: the resulting object should not have the property x

symptom.text: The __proto__ property could be copied during a deep copy operation, potentially leading to prototype pollution.

root_cause.text: The deepCopy function did not check if the property name being processed was '__proto__'.

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe property copying
fix: The deepCopy function was updated to skip the '__proto__' key during the property iteration loop.
guard: The check 'name !== '__proto__'' in the deepCopy function.
lesson: Always sanitize or skip sensitive keys like __proto__ when performing recursive object cloning.

regression.given: a payload containing a '__proto__' property with a 'protoPollution' value
regression.when: util.deepCopy is called with an empty object and the payload
regression.then: the resulting object should not have the 'protoPollution' property on its prototype

symptom.text: Properties could be injected into the prototype of Object, Number, String, or Array via command line arguments.

root_cause.text: The setKey function allowed traversing into and modifying prototype objects when keys matched '__proto__' or pointed to built-in prototypes.

pattern: prototype pollution via object property injection
fix: The setKey function was updated to explicitly check for and skip '__proto__' keys and to reset target objects to new objects or arrays if they point to built-in prototypes.
guard: The check 'if (key === '__proto__') return;' in setKey.
lesson: Prevent modification of built-in prototypes when performing deep property assignment.

regression.given: Arguments containing '__proto__' or paths targeting built-in prototypes like Array.prototype
regression.then: the prototype of built-in objects remains unpolluted

symptom.text: Prototype pollution could occur when parsing arguments with keys like __proto__.

root_cause.text: The parser allowed the use of the __proto__ key when creating nested objects via dot notation.

pattern: prototype pollution via object key manipulation
fix: The sanitizeKey function was introduced to rename '__proto__' to '___proto___' during the parsing of keys.
guard: sanitizeKey
lesson: Sanitize user-controlled keys to prevent prototype pollution when building objects.

regression.given: parser is called with arguments containing __proto__ in dot notation or as a standalone flag
regression.then: the resulting object should contain ___proto___ instead of __proto__ and the global Object prototype should remain unpolluted

symptom.text: A tarball could contain files that, when extracted, are placed outside the intended collection installation directory.

root_cause.text: The extraction process did not validate if the destination path of a tar entry remained within the target collection directory.

pattern: path traversal via archive extraction
fix: Added a check in _extract_tar_file to ensure the absolute destination path of the file is within the target directory.
guard: The check in _extract_tar_file using os.path.abspath and comparing b_parent_dir against b_dest.
lesson: Always validate that file paths extracted from archives are contained within the intended destination directory.

regression.given: A tarball containing a file entry with a path component like '../../outside.sh'
regression.then: The installation should fail with an AnsibleError indicating the entry would be placed outside the collection directory

symptom.text: The extraction process could write files or directories outside of the intended output directory, potentially via symlink attacks or path traversal.

root_cause.text: The code did not validate that newly created directories or symlinked destinations remained within the boundaries of the specified output path.

pattern: path traversal via symlink or directory creation
fix: Introduced safeMakeDir and preventWritingThroughSymlink to validate that all real paths remain within the real output path during extraction in extractFile.
guard: safeMakeDir and preventWritingThroughSymlink functions checking realpath boundaries
lesson: Always validate that file system operations are constrained within the intended root directory using real paths.

symptom.text: Authorization headers are leaked to different hostnames during redirects.

root_cause.text: The client does not strip the authorization header when the redirect URL points to a different hostname.

pattern: sensitive credential leakage on cross-origin redirects
fix: In HttpClient, the code now iterates through headers and deletes any header with a case-insensitive name of 'authorization' if the parsedRedirectUrl hostname differs from the parsedUrl hostname.
guard: check if parsedRedirectUrl.hostname !== parsedUrl.hostname in HttpClient
lesson: Strip sensitive authentication credentials when following redirects to a different origin.

regression.given: a request with an Authorization header is made to a URL that redirects to a different hostname
regression.then: the Authorization header is not present in the subsequent request

symptom.text: The client fails to recognize chunked transfer encoding when the encoding header contains multiple values.

root_cause.text: The code only checked if the entire transfer encoding string was equal to chunked.

pattern: improper parsing of comma-separated header values
fix: The setup_body function was updated to split the transfer encoding string by commas and check each part for the chunked value.
guard: the comma-splitting loop in setup_body
lesson: Always account for multiple values in comma-separated HTTP headers.

symptom.text: The zipObjectDeep function could modify the prototype of objects or the global object.

root_cause.text: The function allowed setting properties with keys that match sensitive prototype properties like __proto__, constructor, or prototype.

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe property assignment
fix: The function zipObjectDeep now checks if the key is '__proto__', 'constructor', or 'prototype' and returns the object early if a match is found.
guard: The check for '__proto__', 'constructor', or 'prototype' in zipObjectDeep.
lesson: Always validate or sanitize keys when performing deep property assignments to prevent prototype pollution.

regression.given: keys like '__proto__.a', 'constructor.b', or 'prototype.c' are passed to zipObjectDeep
regression.then: the global object and existing variables are not modified and no new properties are created on the prototype

symptom.text: The unflatten function could potentially modify the prototype of the target object.

root_cause.text: The unflatten function did not check if a key was '__proto__' before processing it.

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe key assignment
fix: Added a check in unflatten to return early if key1 is '__proto__'.
guard: The check for '__proto__' in unflatten.
lesson: Always validate or sanitize keys when performing deep object manipulation to prevent prototype pollution.

symptom.text: unknown

root_cause.text: The parser was tracking read bytes and checking against maxAbortedPayload even for non-aborted requests, and the resume logic was not properly checking for aborted requests in all states.

pattern: improper state management during request abortion
fix: Removed maxAbortedPayload tracking and logic in Parser and Client; updated _resume to check for aborted requests in both running and pending states; updated Request.onConnect to manage timeout timers correctly.
guard: check for request.aborted in _resume and Parser.onUpgrade
lesson: Always verify the validity of a request state before proceeding with operations like resuming or attaching sockets.

regression.given: a client request is aborted
regression.when: the parser processes data or the client resumes
regression.then: the aborted request should not trigger payload limits or continue processing

symptom.text: An attacker could pollute the prototype of an object by setting values via specific JSON pointer keys.

root_cause.text: The set function allowed traversing and modifying sensitive properties like __proto__, prototype, or constructor.

pattern: Prototype pollution via unsafe property access
fix: The api.set function now skips tokens that match __proto__, constructor, or prototype.
guard: The check for tok === "__proto__" || tok === "constructor" || tok === "prototype" in api.set.
lesson: Always validate or block sensitive property names when performing deep object updates.

regression.given: An object and a JSON pointer targeting __proto__, prototype, or constructor
regression.then: The target object remains unpolluted

symptom.text: The socket might not correctly respect back-pressure when the parser determines the body should be paused.

root_cause.text: The parser was using the standard socket.pause and socket.resume methods instead of directly controlling the underlying handle reading state.

pattern: improper use of stream flow control
fix: The Parser class now uses socketPause and socketResume functions which manipulate the underlying handle reading state instead of calling socket.pause and socket.resume.
guard: socketPause and socketResume functions in lib/core/client.js
lesson: Control the underlying resource reading state directly when managing back-pressure in custom parsers.

regression.given: a client request where the body is paused and then resumed
regression.when: the data is piped from a readable source to the response body
regression.then: the internal buffer length should stay below the highWaterMark

symptom.text: An attacker could use crafted filenames within an archive to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.

root_cause.text: The unarchiving processes for Rar, Tar, and Zip did not validate that the extracted file paths remained within the intended destination directory.

pattern: path traversal vulnerability in file extraction
fix: Introduced the FilenameChecker interface and implemented CheckPath in Rar, Tar, and Zip types to validate that the joined destination path starts with the absolute destination directory. The extraction loops in unrarNext, untarNext, and extractNext now call CheckPath and return an error if a traversal attempt is detected.
guard: CheckPath function using filepath.Abs and strings.HasPrefix
lesson: Always validate that file paths extracted from archives are contained within the target destination directory.

symptom.text: magic properties of an object could be set

root_cause.text: the code allowed setting __proto__ or constructor properties

pattern: prototype pollution vulnerability
fix: added a check in the logic to throw an error if currentPath is __proto__ or constructor is being set on a function
guard: check for __proto__ and constructor in the path traversal logic
lesson: prevent modification of sensitive object properties like __proto__ or constructor

symptom.text: The prototype of the object could be polluted when setting or updating locales.

root_cause.text: The cache was initialized as a plain object literal, which inherits from Object.prototype.

pattern: prototype pollution via object property manipulation
fix: Changed the initialization of this.cache in the Y18N constructor to use Object.create(null).
guard: Object.create(null) in the Y18N constructor
lesson: Use null-prototype objects for internal caches to prevent prototype pollution.

regression.given: a y18n instance with locale set to '__proto__'
regression.when: updateLocale is called with a property
regression.then: the property should not be present on the global Object prototype

symptom.text: Parsing INI files could modify the prototype of objects, such as Object.prototype or Array.prototype.

root_cause.text: The parser allowed setting keys named '__proto__' during section parsing, key processing, and nested path traversal.

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe key assignment
fix: The decode function was updated to skip assignment when the section name or key is '__proto__'.
guard: The check 'if (part === '__proto__') return' in the parts traversal loop.
lesson: Always validate or sanitize keys used for object property assignment to prevent prototype pollution.

regression.given: An INI string containing '__proto__' sections or keys like 'kid.__proto__.foo' or '__proto__[
regression.then: the resulting object does not have modified prototypes and Object.prototype remains untouched
